cevap: Three walks this week and feeling "a bit better" today is real, even if it's hard to trust yet. You don't have to know how long it will last to let yourself feel good about it right now.
Staying quiet because "I actually know she's right" sounds like a heavy thing to carry on your own. You're allowed to hold that awareness without it meaning you always have to defend yourself.
It makes sense that "even sitting there listening" could wear you out, showing up takes real energy. Still, leaving feeling lighter is worth holding onto.
"I'm just very tired" is worth saying, even when other people read it as something else. You don't need the perfect words for that to be true.

Evenings sound like the hardest stretch, that restlessness when you "don't know what to do" and reach for your phone. Just noticing that pattern is already something, maybe there's one small thing to try in that gap next time.
Thank you for sharing that here, saying "this actually isn't my first attempt" takes real courage. Having come back before shows you know how to keep going, even when the road isn't a straight line.
"At least I answer the phone now" is a real shift, that's connection finding its way back. Small changes like that can add up to a lot.
It takes honesty to say "I'm actually afraid of being alone" behind what people assume about you. Noticing why you stay out longer is a useful thing to understand about yourself.
Going to bed at eleven "instead of two" is a big change for your body and mind. That kind of steadier rhythm can ripple into how you feel across the whole day.

Feeling like reaching out means "admitting I failed" is a heavy way to see it, but asking for help is really the opposite of that. Whenever you're ready, that conversation will still be there waiting.
Two weeks of eating regularly and your appetite "opened up a bit", that's your body responding to the care you've been giving it. That's genuinely worth noticing.
You showed up even though "I actually didn't want to go", and that still counts, whatever got you there. Sometimes just getting in the car is the hardest part.
